questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have an interest for this part of Europe and I wanted to learn more, and then the price levels of Warsaw compared to other cities effected my choice as well

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The only reason why it isn't 10/10 is because of the university and teaching here

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: very easy, I think the host institution was amazing in helping you upon arrival

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There where a buddy program made by students for Erasmus students and the there were also some group chats from the university and from the local Erasmus student network

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I think the university really did more than you could ever expect to help us, they where available on WhatsApp all the time and did several zoom meetings before the arrival

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived at a dorm, and it was very easy to get, I just signed up for it through the university

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived at a dorm and I would really recommend, it is a great way to meet people and it is also way cheeper than finding housing yourself

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a very confusing process we had to figure out what courses we wanted and be ready at a specific time, because the registration opened in a specific time, and then you had to be really fast and also having some plan b's ready in case the course fills up. Both I think the university was very helpful in informing on the proces

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: zoom meetings, group chats, you could email the university

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: more or less, my problem was that most of the courses I had reapproval for wasn't available, because they only upload the courses for the semester a couple of weeks before start, therefor I had to make many changes in my pre-approvals

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: dont stress to much about the proces with courses before you can also make changes after the semester starts, and it will all work out

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I liked that my uni had special courses for Erasmus students and that they had so many different courses to chose between, but I Think the academic level was low and the teaching not the best

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: the courses were much easier than at home, even the master courses were easy. all teachers present without having sources which made it feel not that academic and the exam were also more easy than at KU

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different. The classes were much smaller and active participation and presentations are a part of your grade. The teacher also check if you are there at every class and if you miss more than one you will fail the course. I like the active participations and the smaller classes also made a very safe learning environment, but it felt a bit like being in highschool again, especially with the checking if we were there

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Comparative politics, comparative political systems, EU law, EU decision-making procedures, Shades of populism, postcolonial discourse of the global south in IR, theories of capitalist imperialism and Polands foreign policy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really recommend shades of populism, it was one of the best courses I have had in all my time at uni, and the professor is great! I also liked Polands foreign policy because you learn a lot about polish history as well

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: none

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: In general we are told that Poland is very cheap, and it is definitely cheeper than Copenhagen, but it is not as cheap as you imagine. I had a cheap rent so I used more on food and personal spending but I think food was more expensive than I thought it would be. Coffee at a cafe is also very expensive for some reason. In general I think the prices are 2/3 af Copenhagen

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My uni had a lot of sport you could join, but as with the courses it was very confusing and you had to be ready at a specific time and they filled up very fast, so I don't think it is easy to get the sport you want. There is not a lot of clubs or places to hang out at the university

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: all kind of sports and academic events

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Warsaw is such a cultural city so I would recommend going to all the museums, theater, cinemas, parks etc. All the museums have a free day during the week

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to some of all the nice cafes and bars, use some of the cultural things at the city. I also traveled to other cities in Poland it was very easy

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: super easy, I dint find it so different in Poland. Warsaw is very much like every other modern european capital and the people are super nice and open

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: go to the orientation week organized by ESN, its a great way to meet people. the first weeks they have multiple event every day and it continues with events every week during the hole semester

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none, but I regret not taking polish classes during my stay, it would have been nice to communicate more in Polish

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the food is great and all the cultural opportunities too. I also had some nice polish friends, and it is a great way to get to know the culture more, so I would recommend taking some courses that aren't only for Erasmus students

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Dont expect that you are going for the academic challenge, but you will learn so much in so many other ways. Its a great city, great culture and history and you will enjoy so much

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be stressed about the process, you are in really good hands

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The relations with people from all over the world, and then I really appreciated to get to learn about Poland by living here

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I didnt have any big challenges, I think everything was great!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
